subject: Banking
title: Too Big to Fail
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Too Big to Fail.

hook.text: In 2008, the US government bailed out banks with $700 billion in taxpayer money. They were deemed too big to let fail.

buildup.text: If a systemically important bank collapses, it drags down every bank it trades with.

discovery.text: TARP funds went to Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, and others.

twist.text: Bankers received billions in bonuses the same year taxpayers bailed them out.

climax.text: Too big to fail means profits are private and losses are public.

punchline.text: $700 billion bailout, billions in bonuses. Losses public, profits private.

quiz.question: What is the 'moral hazard' of too-big-to-fail policies?
options: Banks take excessive risks knowing the government will rescue them
